title: parenthesising the whole callee of a capability read leaves it a capability read: five parenthesised spellings keep their row, are subtracted by a layer, and run
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Context Access': '`Capability.context()` MUST be an inherited, compiler-recognized call on subclasses of `Context`. ... The call is intentionally library-shaped: it uses ordinary static method-call syntax and has ordinary runtime behavior after lowering, while the compiler gives it additional static meaning.' A parenthesis is not part of the call and not part of the receiver; `(Reader.context)()` and `Reader.context()` are the same call to the same function. WHY THIS CASE EXISTS, and it is the one this repository can least afford to lose: `(Reader.context)()` was REFUSED by the Go fork as a detached reference — an over-correction of the rule that legitimately refuses `take(Reader.context)`, and the seventh over-correction this repository has shipped. The two spellings differ by whether a call follows the parenthesis, which is exactly the kind of distinction a syntactic guard collapses. `sound-capability-receivers-keep-their-row-and-run` is this case's cousin and covers parentheses around the RECEIVER (`(Reader).context()`), optional chains, element access and casts; it does not cover a parenthesis around the whole callee, and that gap is what the fork fell into. The five parenthesised spellings here are chosen so that a guard which merely special-cases the shortest one is still caught: a doubled parenthesis, the same callee inside a template substitution, the same callee as a call argument, and the same callee inside a nested arrow — the last because a detached-reference check that walks upward from the member expression has to keep walking through a function boundary correctly. WHY THE OUTPUT IS THE EVIDENCE: `read` upper-cases its key, so every `ADA` is a service instance the layer resolved at run time. A backend that recognized the call statically but lowered it to something that does not consult the provided scope compiles and then panics. WHY ONE LINE IS BRACKETED: `[ADA]` is the call-argument spelling, and having one line differ means a lowering that reordered or duplicated the entries produces something visibly wrong rather than a permutation of six identical strings. WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: the requirement row by inspection, which no corpus expectation can read — only that one `Layer.succeed(Reader, service)` subtracts all six. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the fifth declared stdout line from `[ADA]` to `[ada]` turns the case red on BOTH backends with the stdout diff printed, and the expectation was restored byte-identically (sha256 39a582d07b1468bf0911209d8f9d72b44c24803039a05118228d456bac99b704 before and after, that digest being this file's content at the moment the mutation ran — the sentence recording it is appended afterwards, so the shipped file necessarily hashes differently). The paired refusal control is `a-detached-context-reference-is-refused-in-every-spelling`, which holds the other side of exactly this boundary: `take((Reader.context))` — the SAME parenthesised member expression with no call after it — must stay refused, so a fix that accepts every parenthesised `context` turns that case red rather than passing this one for the wrong reason.
